goal: Reduce full graph encoder inference latency for the standard workload, preserving the full output checks.
completion: One measured invocation completes exactly one full forward of the two-layer mean GraphSAGE encoder over the standard directed multigraph (4096 nodes, 65536 edges) under torch.inference_mode(), returning the complete [4096, 64] float32 output tensor. The source's completion boundary is the CUDA-synchronized wall-clock interval around infer(model, inputs) (infer.py:53-58): torch.cuda.synchronize() before the timer, one model(*inputs) call, torch.cuda.synchronize() before reading the clock. Model/input construction, H2D transfer, the reference/assert_close check, warmup and per-sample statistics queries are outside the measured work.
state_protocol: state holds the eval-mode GraphEncoder on context['device'] and the four GPU-resident input tensors (features [4096,128] fp32, sources [65536] int64, destinations [65536] int64, degree [4096] fp32). Inference is stateless with no cross-invocation state (README.md:19): the forward allocates its own aggregation buffers (zeros_like + index_add_) and consumes no RNG, so reset() is a no-op that restores nothing and leaves the process group intact. run() is a pure function of state; observe() copies the detached full output tensor to CPU. No gradients, optimizer or caches exist. Worker context supplies device/rank/world_size (single process here); no distributed initialization is performed by the adapter.
invariants: Output is the complete [4096, 64] float32 tensor from the full encoder forward; quality compares it with torch.testing.assert_close(atol=1e-05, rtol=1e-4) as in infer.py:44-45.

Model architecture and dimensions are fixed: two MeanSAGE layers, Linear(2*in->out) per layer, input_features=128, hidden_features=256, output_features=64, ReLU between layers (model.py:18-26, workloads.json:2).

Numerical policies: dtype float32, torch.manual_seed(20261021) before weight init, torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest') (infer.py:13-17, workloads.json:9-11).

Input fixture is generated on a separate CPU generator seeded 20261022: randn features [nodes,128], randint sources and destinations in [0,nodes), degree = bincount(destinations, minlength=nodes).float(); duplicated as the source does, then moved to the device (infer.py:19-25).

Graph semantics: directed multigraph on the frozen standard workload (4096 nodes, 65536 edges); duplicate directed edges contribute individually to mean aggregation; nodes without incoming edges get zero neighbor features via zeros-init and degree.clamp_min(1) (README.md:17-19, model.py:12-14).

Timed region is exactly one synchronized full-graph forward with GPU-resident inputs; model/fixture construction, H2D copies, warmup, reference check and peak-memory queries stay outside timing (README.md:13-15, infer.py:49-65).
Inference runs under torch.inference_mode() with no cross-invocation state; each run() is an independent forward over the same inputs (infer.py:28-30).

The objective latency_ms is the source's per-sample wall-clock latency in ms; graphs_per_second = 1000/latency_ms and peak_allocated_bytes = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() are recorded as native-unit metrics without altering the work.
assumptions: request['assets'] is empty because the source declares seeded random fixtures for weights, features and edges (README.md:5-7); the seeded CPU/global generators are the task data, so no pretrained weights or external downloads are needed.
Single-process CUDA execution: context['world_size'] == 1, no process-group work is created by the adapter, and there is no required communication for this workload.

The framework's elapsed_ms (CUDA-synchronized timer around run) has the same semantics as the source's latency_ms sample field, so metrics() reports elapsed_ms directly as the objective and queries CUDA peak stats outside the timer, mirroring infer.py:59-60.

The held-out workload unseen_graph (7168 nodes, 143360 edges) and the secondary memory goal in workloads.json:14-15 are not part of this frozen request and are therefore not implemented by the adapter; the memory-related metrics are still reported as informational values.
observe() returns the full output tensor (detached, on CPU) as the only required correctness observation; request['required_observations'] is empty and no discrete outputs exist.
The adapter reuses inputs/source/model.py unmodified via a local sys.path entry; only adapter.py and understanding.json are written.
